The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(v_p(x)\) denote the exponent of prime \(p\) in \(x\).

A move replaces a pair \((a,b)\) by \((\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b))\). For each prime \(p\), the exponents \((v_p(a),v_p(b))\) are replaced by
\[
(\min(v_p(a),v_p(b)),\max(v_p(a),v_p(b))).
\]
So for each prime \(p\), the multiset of \(p\)-adic exponents on the board is invariant.

Also, the product of all numbers is invariant. If a move actually changes the board, write \(a=gx,\ b=gy\) with \(\gcd(x,y)=1\) and \(x,y>1\). Then
\[
\gcd(a,b)+\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)-(a+b)
=g(1+xy-x-y)=g(x-1)(y-1)>0.
\]
Thus the sum of the board entries strictly increases on every changing move, and since the product is fixed, only finitely many boards are possible. Hence the process always reaches a terminal board.

At termination, no pair can be changed, so every two numbers on the board are comparable by divisibility. Sorting the final numbers as
\[
x_1\le x_2\le \cdots \le x_{2100},
\]
we have
\[
x_1\mid x_2\mid \cdots \mid x_{2100}.
\]
Therefore, for each prime \(p\), the sequence
\[
v_p(x_1),v_p(x_2),\dots,v_p(x_{2100})
\]
is nondecreasing. Since the multiset of \(p\)-adic exponents is the original multiset, \(v_p(x_i)\) must be the \(i\)-th smallest value of \(v_p(1),v_p(2),\dots,v_p(2100)\).

We need the 2026th smallest final number, which is \(x_{2026}\). The 2026th smallest is the
\[
2100-2026+1=75
\]
th largest for each prime exponent.

For a prime \(p\), the number of integers among \(1,\dots,2100\) with \(v_p\ge t\) is
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^t}\right\rfloor.
\]
Thus the 75th largest exponent is the largest \(t\) such that
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^t}\right\rfloor\ge 75.
\]
Since \(2100/75=28\), this is equivalent to
\[
p^t\le 28.
\]

Now list the relevant primes:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
p & \text{exponent in }x_{2026}\\ \hline
2 & 4 \quad (2^4\le28<2^5)\\
3 & 3 \quad (3^3=27\le28<3^4)\\
5 & 2 \quad (5^2=25\le28<5^3)\\
7,11,13,17,19,23 & 1 \quad (p\le28<p^2)\\
p\ge29 & 0
\end{array}
\]

Therefore
\[
x_{2026}=2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]

The number of positive divisors is
\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot4\cdot3\cdot64
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
